annotations.keyFindings: In 2,340 children linked to provincial emergency data, a complete plan was associated with fewer 90-day emergency revisits (adjusted hazard ratio 0.72, 95 percent CI 0.58 to 0.89); complete plans were issued at 52 percent of discharges.
annotations.limitations: Observational; family engagement not measured; four hospitals in another province with a different template.
annotations.notes: Closest in design to the proposed study; sets planning values.

annotations.keyFindings: A discharge checklist with weekly feedback raised plan completeness from 48 to 86 percent; 30-day revisits changed from 11 to 9 percent, compatible with chance.
annotations.limitations: Uncontrolled before-and-after on one ward; 210 and 196 discharges in the two periods; no adjustment for season.

annotations.keyFindings: Across seven randomised trials, written action plans reduced urgent care visits (risk ratio 0.78, 95 percent CI 0.64 to 0.95); no study measured plan completeness.
annotations.limitations: Plans usually delivered with education; heterogeneity; search ended in 2019.

annotations.keyFindings: A five-item completeness score for scanned plans had good agreement between two scorers (kappa 0.81), lowest for the yellow-zone item (kappa 0.64); 38 percent of plans were fully complete.
annotations.limitations: One hospital's template; two scorers only.

annotations.keyFindings: Caregivers preferring a language other than English gave correct yellow-zone steps in 44 percent of teach-back tasks against 79 percent of English-preferring caregivers.
annotations.limitations: One hospital; no revisit outcomes; teach-back done by study staff.

annotations.keyFindings: Of 90-day asthma revisits after a paediatric discharge, 21 percent occurred at another hospital, more often for children from the lowest income quintile.
annotations.limitations: Two children's hospitals; administrative diagnosis codes.

annotations.keyFindings: In 11 of 14 observational studies, children who received a discharge intervention differed in severity or family engagement markers; a minimum adjustment set and a negative control outcome are proposed.

claims.text: In a provincial cohort of 2,340 children discharged after an asthma admission, a complete written action plan was associated with fewer emergency revisits within 90 days (adjusted hazard ratio 0.72).

claims.interpretation: An association of this size is plausible and gives a planning value; it may partly reflect family engagement.

claims.text: About one in five asthma emergency revisits within 90 days of a paediatric discharge took place at a hospital other than the discharging one.
claims.passage: Of these revisits, 21 percent took place at a hospital other than the discharging one
claims.interpretation: Single-hospital data would under-count the outcome, most among lower-income families; linkage is needed.

claims.interpretation: Confounding by severity and engagement is the main threat; adjust for prior admissions and controller use and add a negative control outcome.

synthesis: Seven retrieved records, appraised at abstract level. One provincial cohort found fewer 90-day emergency revisits after a complete plan (adjusted hazard ratio 0.72), and a review of seven trials supports written plans in general, though no trial measured completeness. A reliable five-item completeness score exists. One fifth of revisits happen at other hospitals, so linkage to provincial data is needed, and observational studies of discharge interventions are prone to confounding by severity and engagement. Caregivers who prefer another language understand English plans less well. The evidence supports a linked cohort with a pre-specified adjustment set, not a claim that completeness causes fewer revisits.
gradeRationale: One directly relevant observational cohort, a review of trials that did not measure completeness, and single-site measurement and equity studies; consistent direction but serious risk of confounding and indirectness.
summary: Seven retrieved records appraised; five source-derived claims with passages; overall certainty low.
